plan.question: Does current complete-suite cost remain dominated by fixed runner/owner work, or repeated per-test work, as suite size increases?
plan.scope: Diagnostic scaling of one unchanged controlled body through existing configuration counts; not original acceptance scenario observations at larger sizes. Preserve the original nine-scenario final matrix.
plan.preflight: Four 15-test captures, both engines and both workers, before timing.
plan.controls: Exact original workload bytes; dynamic expected title set, count, original storage/trusted-event/view/focus/version observations, distinct fresh context reports, worker process/slot stability, native launch receipts, fixture request counts and natural drain.
plan.analysis: Report each capture and each size ratio. A descriptive affine fit can suggest fixed/repeated cost; intercept is not an independently measured startup interval or guaranteed removable work. No acceptance threshold and no final performance claim.

limitations: Only the setup family is scaled through the existing configuration; test body bytes are unchanged. Larger counts are additional diagnostic workloads, not replacements for original acceptance scenarios.
Two reversed blocks provide observations, not eight-pair confidence acceptance.
Endpoint slopes and extrapolated intercepts are descriptive; they do not isolate CPU subsystems, directly measure startup, or estimate guaranteed removable work.
Cgroup CPU deltas and memory peak cover the enclosing diagnostic service interval; full final resource custody is not established.
Warmup-labelled tests remain counted in complete work. No test or capture is discarded.

decision.reason: Relative advantage shrinks as test count grows; repeated per-test work must fall substantially. At four workers, endpoint CPU increments divided by four nearly match elapsed increments.
decision.nextDirection: Evaluate combined repeated initialization and retirement cost removal rather than repeat startup-only tuning.
